reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend with holidays and reuses it everywhere for moving dates, but the new daily-skip rule is not given a shared definition and app.ts re-expresses the weekend-or-holiday predicate instead of using the (unexported) isWeekendOrHoliday.

duplication.why: The 'daily skips, others move, off means unchanged' dispatch is written three times (getNextDate while-loop, getUpcomingDates filter/map, getDatesInRange flatMap) and the weekend-or-holiday predicate is inlined twice in app.ts.

placement.why: Holiday matching and the moving rule live correctly in shared/schedules.ts, but the daily-skip decision is placed separately in the server handlers and in getNextDate rather than in one shared date-adjustment function; the budget template gets its own local wrapper.

scope.why: Edits stay within schedule date handling, the new handler and their tests; the RecurConfig/parseRecurDate additions are required for the feature.

maintainability.why: A future change to how weekend/holiday occurrences are treated must be made consistently in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and the budget template's helper, which already diverge (the template has no daily-skip branch).

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange compute `!d.isWeekend(date) && !isHoliday(...)` and the daily-skip branching themselves instead of a shared helper used by getNextDate.

disguised_duplication.where: The same skip-or-move dispatch appears as a while loop in shared getNextDate, a ternary of filter/map in getUpcomingDates and a flatMap in getDatesInRange; the weekend-or-holiday check is isWeekendOrHoliday in shared but an inline conjunction in app.ts.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains a daily-frequency special branch; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template's getAdjustedScheduleDate each re-implement the adjustment dispatch around the helper.
